terra.problem: The final two sentences repeat the same point without adding explanation or personality.
John describes something like a sea of glass, not an unqualified sea of glass.
The explanation calls it a sea of glass without preserving John's qualification that it was something like one.
The comparison calls what John saw a sea, although he says it was something like a sea of glass. Exodus 15:1 also does not say Moses and Israel sang beside the sea.
David's identification as Israel's king is a Bible fact from outside the passage and needs a reference.
The claim that Elijah stood up to Israel's kings is from outside the passage and needs a reference.
John describes something like a sea, but the explanation calls it a sea without that qualification.
Explaining that a bowl is something to pour from is flat and adds little to the answer.
The claim about trumpets elsewhere in Revelation needs a reference outside this passage.
The claim about crowns elsewhere in Revelation needs a reference outside this passage.
The text says no one could enter the temple; it does not say a door was shut.
The explanation calls what John saw a sea of glass, rather than something like one.
Saying he will not joke about the verse comments on how Papa tells the passage.
Saying they will read the verse plainly comments on how Papa tells the passage.
The angel and the altar do not use the same words about God's judgments, even though their statements agree.
Saying the verse is meant to be hard to read adds a purpose the text does not give.
The bowl is poured on the beast's throne, but the text says its kingdom is plunged into darkness.
The explanation repeats the stated purpose without adding a distinctive voice or further explanation.
The last sentence merely restates that the quotation answers the question, leaving the explanation generic.
Saying the temple is still on the baker's mind assumes something Papa has not been told.

The text compares the earthquake with those since people were on earth, not all of earth's history. It also lists the lightning, rumblings, thunder and quake without saying the first three preceded it.
The verse does not mention celebration, but it does not say nobody is celebrating.
Saying rebuilding would come later introduces an outcome the passage does not give.
The explanation repeats who receives the cup without adding anything beyond the quotation.
The passage describes the hail falling and men cursing God, but does not say the cursing happened after the hail stopped.
